summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for fevers following a recent AV fistula revision. She developed postoperative fatigue, vomiting, and fever, prompting evaluation. Initial labs showed elevated inflammatory markers and transaminitis. Blood cultures were negative to date, and she remained afebrile after 24 hours without antibiotics. Her symptoms were attributed to likely transient bacteremia or viral illness. She also reported worsening exertional shortness of breath; chest imaging showed no acute process, and a stress test was ordered. Abdominal ultrasound revealed 1 cm common bile duct dilation, previously noted intermittently, with plans for outpatient MRCP. She improved clinically, returned to baseline, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged in primary care, cardiology, and gastroenterology.
